title: How could anyone draw a perfect circle?
description: A pattern made only of straight lines and round circles opens the chapter. One circle drawn by bare hand wobbles and its ends do not meet, and the video stops on the open question of how such exact shapes could be drawn.
teaching_notes: One idea: a hand cannot draw a perfectly round circle, so we need something better. Ask each child to guess what they would use, and do not confirm any guess, because the next topic settles it. Watch for students who say a circle by hand is good enough.

source: Why a hand cannot draw a perfect circle
video_script.why: Before any instrument is named, the child meets the real problem: a hand drawn circle is uneven, yet the artwork in the book is exact.
video_script.substitution: Picture a circle drawn with bare hands, then the same circle drawn perfectly round.
video_script.anchor: The artwork pictures of the chapter, made only of straight lines and perfectly round circles
maths_rules: The pattern uses straight lines and circles only; no length or angle is shown.
The hand drawn circle wobbles and its two ends do not meet; it is never corrected on screen.
The open question is how such exact circles and lines could be drawn; it is never answered or hinted.
video_script.design: One idea: a hand cannot draw an exact circle. Assumes nothing. The pattern stays to the end; no hard clear.
